1880: Bahrain accepts British protection.
1886: the Aden Protectorate begins with the Mahra.
1890: the rest of the hinterland comes under protection.
6-8 March 1892: the Trucial Coast comes under British protection.
5 November 1914: the occupation of Cyprus ends in annexation (next event).
5 November 1914: Britain annexes Cyprus.
1917: British forces conquer southern Ottoman Syria.
13 November 1918: British troops enter Constantinople.
6 December 1918: the British enter Cologne.

25 April 1920: Britain is assigned the mandate for Palestine.
1922: Transjordan is set apart under the mandate.
6 December 1922: the Irish Free State leaves the United Kingdom.
4 October 1923: the Allies leave Constantinople.
January 1926: the British leave the Cologne zone.
1927: the state is renamed the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

7 July 1941: the United States takes over Iceland's defence.

November 1967: the Colony of Aden is given up.

wars.name: Napoleonic Wars
wars.outcome: Britain took Zakynthos and Kefalonia (1809) and Lefkada (1810) and obtained 'a protectorate over the Ionian Islands' by the Treaty of Paris of 5 November 1815; Malta was confirmed by the 1814 Treaty of Paris.

wars.name: World War I
wars.outcome: Cyprus annexed after the Ottomans 'joined the Central Powers' (5 November 1914), southern Syria conquered in 1917, Constantinople and the Cologne zone occupied after the Armistice of 11 November 1918.

wars.name: Chanak Crisis
wars.outcome: 'The British decided to resist any attempt to penetrate the neutral zone of the Straits'; the crisis 'nearly resulted in hostilities, these being avoided on 11 October 1922' (Armistice of Mudanya).

wars.name: World War II
wars.outcome: British occupation of Iceland ('Operation Fork', 10 May 1940) handed to the United States on 7 July 1941; the British zone of Germany from June 1945.

wars.name: Jebel Akhdar War
wars.outcome: No border moved: the Imam Ghalib Bin Ali 'started an uprising in 1954'; 'In 1957, British forces bombarded the town of Nizwa'; 'the last rebel forces were defeated two years later, in 1959'.

certainty.note: The coast, the Irish border from 1922 and the enclaves (Gibraltar, Malta, Aden, Cyprus after 1914) are fixed lines.
